items.note: ⚠ OCR. Editor's profile of Bhoja: Paramara king of Dhara, father Sindhula (some say Sindhuraja), title Ranaranga-malla, mother Savitri, son Jayasimha.
items.gloss: Bhoja, the Paramara lord of Dhara: his father's name is Sindhula, whom some call Sindhuraja. One name of Bhoja was Ranaranga-malla (probably a title). Bhoja's mother was named Savitri. His son was Jayasimha.

items.note: ⚠ OCR. Bhoja moved his capital from Avantika and founded Dhara; built a Sarasvati temple there; probably a Shaiva judging from his invocation verses.
items.gloss: Bhoja moved the capital from Avantika and founded the city of Dhara, full of historical remains. The learning-loving Bhoja built a Sarasvati temple there with a Sarasvati image, now in a museum in England. Bhoja was probably a Shaiva, as inferred from his invocatory verses.

items.note: ⚠ OCR. Bhoja's liberality was famous; several copper-plates found; builder of temples such as Bhojesvara and Rameshvara.
items.gloss: Bhoja's generosity is famous. Several of his copper-plates have been found. From the works of Merutunga, Ballalasena and others his wide fame is known. He was the builder of many temples, such as Bhojeshvara and Rameshvara.

items.note: ⚠ OCR. Bhoja's reign usually taken as Samvat 1075-1110 (c. 1018-1054 CE), with evidence he lived to 1062 CE.
items.gloss: Bhoja's period is certain; historians generally take his reign as Samvat 1075-1110 (1018-1054 CE). There is evidence he was alive until 1062 CE (Keith, History of Sanskrit Literature, p. 153).
refs: Keith, History of Sanskrit Literature, p. 153

items.gloss: This grammar is the Sarasvatikanthabharana. The Patanjala vritti is a commentary on the Yoga-sutra, not on the Mahabhashya. The commentary's proper name is 'Rajamartanda-vritti'.
